name: Extension
description: What installing a guest idiom with an optional host backend composes, and what stands behind its path.

scenarios.title: The idiom becomes a snippet under the Extension's name
given: an Extension named `File` carrying mruby source
scenarios.then: the snippet table holds one entry named `File`

scenarios.title: The backend is bound where it says, not where the Extension is named
given: an Extension named `File` whose backend declares the path `Vfs`
scenarios.then: the backend object is bound at `Vfs`

scenarios.title: An idiom with nothing behind it binds nothing
given: an Extension carrying source and no backend
scenarios.then: no Service is bound

scenarios.title: Install chains
given: an Extension carrying source
scenarios.then: it answers the registry it was called on

scenarios.title: A method the idiom implements stays in the guest
given: an installed Extension whose source defines a method needing no host
scenarios.then: it answers without a dispatch to the host

scenarios.title: A method the idiom cannot answer reaches the backend
given: an installed Extension whose backend is bound to a host object
scenarios.when: guest code calls a method the idiom routes to that backend
scenarios.then: the host object's answer reaches the guest

scenarios.title: An idiom is useful without a backend
given: an installed Extension carrying source and no backend
scenarios.when: guest code calls a method needing no host
scenarios.then: it answers

scenarios.title: An unbacked idiom fails closed where it needs the host
given: an installed Extension carrying source and no backend
scenarios.when: guest code calls a method the idiom routes to a backend
scenarios.then: `Kobako::ServiceError` is raised

scenarios.title: A backend declaring `object:` is bound at install
given: an Extension whose backend declares `object:`
scenarios.then: that object is bound at the backend's path

scenarios.title: A backend declaring `object:` takes no part in per-invocation resolution
given: an installed Extension whose backend declares `object:`
scenarios.then: the resolution carries no entry for that path

scenarios.title: A backend declaring `provider:` holds its path before the first resolution
given: an Extension whose backend declares `provider:`
scenarios.then: the path is bound to the `Kobako::Unresolved` sentinel

scenarios.title: A backend declaring `provider:` yields a fresh object per invocation
given: an installed Extension whose backend declares `provider:`
scenarios.when: a second invocation resolves its backends
scenarios.then: the path carries a different object than the first resolution gave it

scenarios.title: A backend declares one kind or the other
given: a backend declaration carrying both `object:` and `provider:`
scenarios.then: `ArgumentError` is raised

scenarios.title: A backend declaring neither keyword is a fillable
given: an Extension whose backend declares neither `object:` nor `provider:`
scenarios.then: the path is bound to the `Kobako::Unresolved` sentinel

scenarios.title: A fillable waits to be filled rather than resolved
given: an installed Extension whose backend declares neither keyword
scenarios.then: the resolution carries no entry for that path

scenarios.title: One provider value is one resource
given: two installed Extensions whose backends declare the same `provider:` value
scenarios.then: the provider has been called once

scenarios.title: A shared provider backs every path it was given to
given: two installed Extensions whose backends declare the same `provider:` value
scenarios.then: both paths carry the same object

scenarios.title: Distinct providers are distinct resources
given: two installed Extensions whose backends declare different `provider:` values
scenarios.then: the two paths carry different objects

scenarios.title: A provider's failure is the Host App's own
given: an installed Extension whose `provider:` raises
scenarios.then: the provider's own exception reaches the caller unwrapped

scenarios.title: A provider's failure does not settle the Sandbox
given: an installed Extension whose `provider:` raised on its first call and succeeds afterward
an invocation that failed on that resolution
scenarios.when: a later invocation resolves its backends
scenarios.then: the path carries the object the provider yielded

scenarios.title: A fixed backend accumulates across invocations
given: an installed Extension whose backend declares `object:` over a stateful host object
an invocation that wrote to it through the guest idiom
scenarios.when: a later invocation reads that value through the same idiom
scenarios.then: the written value comes back

scenarios.title: A per-invocation backend accumulates nothing
given: an installed Extension whose backend declares `provider:` over a stateful host object
an invocation that wrote to it through the guest idiom
scenarios.when: a later invocation reads that value through the same idiom
scenarios.then: the value is absent

scenarios.title: A satisfied dependency passes the seal
given: two installed Extensions, one declaring the other in `depends_on`
scenarios.then: the seal answers its registry

scenarios.title: A dependency is matched as a name, not as a spelling
given: two installed Extensions whose `depends_on` entry and name are written in different String and Symbol forms
scenarios.then: the seal answers its registry

scenarios.title: Presence is all that is asserted, so cycles stand
given: two installed Extensions each declaring the other in `depends_on`
scenarios.then: the seal answers its registry

scenarios.title: The dependency assertion is a gate, not a recurring check
given: a registry that has sealed once
an Extension added afterward whose `depends_on` names nothing installed
scenarios.then: the seal answers its registry

scenarios.title: Every idiom is in place before any of them runs
given: two installed Extensions, the dependent one installed first, whose source names the other's constant
scenarios.when: guest code calls the dependent Extension's method
scenarios.then: it answers with the value read from the other Extension's constant

text: Installing an Extension is observable in two places: what the composition
leaves behind — a snippet under one name, a Service under another — and
what stands behind that path once an invocation begins, which the backend's
declared keyword decides. The dependency scenarios cover the third: when
that composition is checked, and how little the check asks.
Installing after the seal, an unmet dependency, and a malformed Extension
all raise, so they belong to the error taxonomy and are specified there.
The `File` idiom the end-to-end witnesses install is an illustrative fixture
— kobako ships no concrete Extension — so no scenario here states what that
idiom does, only what installing one produces.
